analysis.title: Where are the opportunities in fixed income?
key_insights: UBS CIO views fixed income as Attractive. It favors selective exposure to short- and medium-duration high-quality bonds for income, potential price gains and diversification.
The 10-year US Treasury yield is around 5.13%, up about 100 basis points year to date and below the multi-decade high set in early October. The 10-year German Bund yield stood at 3.38%.
Yields are kept elevated by inflation worries, persistent fiscal concerns and rising hyperscaler debt issuance.
Stronger US inflation data and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary pushed yields higher last week. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 29 basis points and the 2-year yield rose 37 basis points.
UBS is more cautious on the longest-dated bonds because of fiscal sustainability concerns, growing AI-related debt issuance and the potential for term premiums to remain elevated.
Elevated starting yields give a carry cushion against further increases that was not available in 2022. They have historically been a good indication of subsequent total returns.

UBS likes select exposure to emerging market credit and high yield debt for income and diversification. EM sovereign yields are around 7.1% and EM corporate yields around 7% (JPMorgan EMBI and CEMBI), which UBS says should underpin high-single-digit returns over 12 months.

Investors should focus less on identifying the peak in yields and more on using current starting yields to strengthen income and diversification. Income-focused investors may prefer shorter maturities to reduce duration risk.
In low-rate economies such as Switzerland, UBS sees merit in equity income approaches and select structured strategies.
